sentences.text: Brachypterygius is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur known from the Late Jurassic of England.
Friedrich von Huene named the genus in 1922 because of the short and wide forepaddle.
This medium-sized ichthyosaur had a body length up to 4 meters.
The forepaddle likely possessed five or six digits, with a maximum phalangeal count between 8 and 16.
While the holotype was originally thought to come from the Lias Group of Bath, evidence suggests it likely originated from the Kimmeridgian Kimmeridge Clay of Kimmeridge Bay, Dorset.
In 1840, Owen erected Ichthyosaurus trigonus based on a single dorsal vertebra found in the Kimmeridge Clay of Westbrook, Wiltshire.
McGowan named the species Grendelius mordax in 1976 based on a large skull discovered in the Kimmeridge Clay of Stowbridge, Norfolk.
Efimov named the genus Otschevia pseudoscythia in 1998 based on a single holotype specimen from the Upper Tithonian of Ulyanovsk in the Volga region of Russia.
Maisch and Matzke considered two Russian species to be synonyms in 2000 and referred them to the new combination Brachypterygius pseudoscythius.
Brachypterygius is closely related to the genera Platypterygius and Caypullisaurus.
Brachypterygius lived during the Late Jurassic period.
Fossils of Brachypterygius have been found in England and European Russia.
Brachypterygius lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
A 2015 study by Zverkov and colleagues argued that Grendelius mordax is distinct enough from Brachypterygius extremus to warrant classification as a separate genus and species.
